name: Odoric of Pordenone dictates his Itinerarium
summary: Franciscan friar Odoric of Pordenone returns from a sixteen-year journey via Trebizond, Persia, the Persian Gulf, India, Sumatra, Java, southern China, and Khanbaliq, where he is reported to have lived for three years among the Franciscan community. Dictates his account to Brother William of Solagna at Padua in 1330; dies the following year.

_quarry.structural_significance: Most-read Latin Christian travelogue of the 14th century outside Marco Polo. Odoric's reports on Hangzhou ('greatest city in the world'), sati in India, and Sumatran cannibalism passed into the compilation later known as The Travels of Sir John Mandeville (c. 1357), shaping European geographical imagination of Asia through the early modern period.
